sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Stephenson County?
sections.html:
Stephenson County splits the work between three desks in Freeport. The Treasurer and Collector sends and takes payment on bills, at the Stewart Centre, 50 West Douglas Street, Suite 503 (fifth floor), 815-235-8264, open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The treasurer's page states plainly that the office does not set assessed values, exemptions or bill amounts.

  • Assessment questions, exemptions, mapping, address clarifications and assessment complaints: the Assessor's office, 815-235-8260.
  • Redemption amounts after a tax sale: the County Clerk, 815-235-8289.
  • Filing a complaint: the clerk of the Board of Review, 50 West Douglas Street, Suite 502.

One local wrinkle matters for owners inside the city. Freeport Township assesses its own parcels, and their numbers begin with 18. The county assessor handles the other 17 townships. The Freeport Township Assessor is at 524 W. Stephenson St., Suite 214, 815-232-6131.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Stephenson County itself?
sections.html:
Stephenson County is the northwestern Illinois county whose seat and largest city is Freeport. It was formed in 1837 from land that had belonged to Jo Daviess and Winnebago counties, and the first settler, in 1832, founded Waddams Grove. Today it covers 565 square miles and touches the Wisconsin line at Green and Lafayette counties.

The 2020 census counted 44,630 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 43,220. Of the county's 21,369 housing units, 10.2 percent were vacant, and among occupied homes 70.4 percent were owner-occupied. The median age is 45.9. About 54 percent of residents live in urban areas and 46 percent in rural ones.

January days in Freeport average a high of 25 and a low of 9 degrees, and July highs reach about 82. Cold winters put furnace age and roof condition high on a buyer's list. The county's public high schools are Freeport, Lena-Winslow, Dakota, Pearl City and Orangeville, with Aquin Catholic as the private option.

sections.h2: When are Stephenson County property taxes due?
sections.html:
For 2025 taxes payable in 2026, the first installment was due Friday, June 26 and the second Friday, September 4. The final day to pay real estate taxes was Monday, November 9. A single bill goes out in May covering both halves, and both can be paid together by the first date.

Stephenson County Treasurer dates for 2025 taxes payable in 2026
DateWhat it marks
May 26, 2026Online lookup and payment opened
June 26, 2026First installment due
September 4, 2026Second installment due
November 9, 2026Last day to pay real estate taxes

The county's FAQ says an installment is on time if the post office postmarks it by midnight of the due date, and a metered postage machine does not count. The county asks mailers to allow for processing time. The last day before the tax sale works differently: payments must be received, not just postmarked, by the end of that business day. Partial payments are returned, because Illinois law does not allow the collector to accept them.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Stephenson County tax bill?
sections.html:
The treasurer accepts payment five ways. A barcoded coupon is needed whether you use the original bill or a reprint, and banks will ask for it too.

  • By mail to Stephenson County Collector, 50 W. Douglas St., Suite 503, Freeport, IL 61032.
  • In the payment dropbox just inside the Stewart Centre lobby. Cash does not go in the box.
  • In person at the treasurer's office on the fifth floor.
  • At most banks in the county. Fifth Third Bank and credit unions cannot take them.
  • Online through the county portal or your bank's bill pay. E-check carries a flat $2.95 fee that covers up to 99 payments, and none of the fees go to the county.

A lost bill can be printed free from the portal. An exact duplicate costs $1.00 per parcel for an owner and $5.00 for anyone else, and veterans pay no duplicate fee. Failing to receive a bill does not cancel the tax or the penalty, so call the Assessor's office at 815-235-8260 if the mailing address is wrong.

sections.h2: How does Stephenson County work out the amount of a bill?
sections.html:
Every bill multiplies a taxable value by a rate. The value starts with the property's worth on January 1 of the tax year, and assessors aim for one-third of fair market value. The county reported a 33.33 percent median level of assessment in a recent publication. Exemptions are subtracted from that assessed value.

The rate depends on where the parcel sits. The county has 104 tax districts, and each parcel lies in its own mix of school, township, road, fire, park, library and county bodies. The county clerk's extension division divides each body's levy by its tax base. The county's page lists these exemptions, among others:

  • Owner Occupied Exemption.
  • Senior Citizen Homestead Exemption and Senior Citizen Freeze.
  • Homestead Improvement Exemption.
  • Disabled Veteran Exemption.

More than 26,000 bills go out each year. Property is taxed, not the person, and the bill is based on the prior year's assessment for a full calendar year.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Stephenson County assessment?
sections.html:
Talk to the township assessor or the chief county assessment office first. If that does not settle it, a written complaint goes to the Board of Review within 30 calendar days after the change list for your township is published (35 ILCS 200/16-55). After that date the board cannot take complaints for that township.

Forms and instructions come from the assessment office at 815-235-8260, in person or online, and the completed form goes to the clerk of the Board of Review. A complaint mailed through the post office counts as filed on its postmark date. The county's own notices say the board is barred by law from accepting late ones.

Someone unhappy with the board's decision can appeal to the Property Tax Appeal Board within 30 days after written notice of that decision, or go to circuit court (35 ILCS 200/16-160). The complaint covers value only. Rates and bill totals are set elsewhere.

sections.h2: What happens if Stephenson County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
A penalty of 1.5 percent per month starts after each due date, and it is not prorated for part of a month. Section 21-15 of the Property Tax Code sets the same rate for counties of this size.

In October, certified letters go to owners of unpaid parcels, and a notice runs in the Village Voices. The unpaid taxes are offered at a November tax sale. The sale auctions the tax, not the house, and a buyer who wins takes a lien at the interest rate bid. Afterward the delinquent records move to the County Clerk, 815-235-8289, who quotes redemption amounts.

The treasurer's FAQ says a home is at risk only if nothing clears the lien in 30 months. For certificates issued on or after January 1, 2024, 35 ILCS 200/21-350 gives 3 years from the date of sale in most cases, so ask the clerk which period covers your parcel.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when a Stephenson County house sells?
sections.html:
The county's FAQ states that prorating between buyer and seller is generally done at closing and written into the contract. Until it is paid, the current owner is liable for the whole amount due. A house with a balance can still be sold, because the title company deducts the tax from the seller's proceeds.

Before you list, take these steps:

  • Print the parcel's history from the county portal, which goes back to the 2000 tax year for most parcels.
  • Ask the treasurer for the exact penalty on any late installment, since the amount is also shown on each payment coupon.
  • Check with your mortgage company whether it pays from escrow. If it does, a lender at fault for a late payment bears the penalty.
  • Confirm with the Assessor that exemptions on the parcel are current.

A Stephenson County house can sell as is for cash, and any tax due is settled from the proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: When is the last day to pay Stephenson County property taxes?
faqs.a: For 2025 taxes payable in 2026, it was Monday, November 9. The two installments were due June 26 and September 4, and a 1.5 percent monthly penalty applied after each.

faqs.q: Who sets my Stephenson County property tax bill?
faqs.a: No single office does. Assessors set values, taxing bodies set levies, and the county clerk calculates rates. The Treasurer only collects and says it cannot change assessed values, exemptions or amounts.

faqs.q: Can I pay half of my Stephenson County bill at a time?
faqs.a: You can pay by installment, but not a partial amount. The two equal installments are due in June and September, and Illinois law bars the collector from taking a payment smaller than a full installment.

faqs.q: Does Freeport Township use the county assessor?
faqs.a: No. Freeport Township assesses its own parcels, and their numbers start with 18. The county assessor covers the other 17 townships, so Freeport owners call the township office at 815-232-6131.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Stephenson County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 30 calendar days after the change list for your township is published. After that the Board of Review cannot accept the complaint, and a later appeal to the state board needs a board decision first.
